Part of the guidelines for translating ancient texts (translation-guidelines.md), split out of it on 2026-10-21 to keep the core file lean. Section number §10, as in the guidelines.

10. Tools (tools/)

Script What Usage
ebl_fetch.py Downloads an eBL corpus chapter and builds reading-edition.md, glossary.md, manuscripts.md, bibliography.md, chapter.atf. Caches in _raw/. python3 -I tools/ebl_fetch.py --list · python3 -I tools/ebl_fetch.py L 1 4 "Standard Babylonian" XI sources/eBL/Gilgamesh-SB-XI
etcsl2md.py ETCSL TEI XML → Markdown (Unicode transliteration, subscript indices). python3 -I tools/etcsl2md.py <c-or-t.xml> <out.md> [url]
cdl2md.py ORACC CDL JSON (from a project zip) → Markdown with lemmatization. python3 -I tools/cdl2md.py <zip> <member> <out.md> <title> <url>
dfhg2md.py DFHG API JSON (Greek fragments) → Markdown. python3 -I tools/dfhg2md.py <in.json> <out.md> <title> <api-url> [frags]

More tools (2026-10-16):

  • check_bible_quotes.py: checks every backticked, vocalized Bible quotation that is followed by a reference against תנך-מנוקד/. It normalizes Unicode, allows prefixes and quotations that run on into the next verses, and defaults to Genesis. python3 -I tools/check_bible_quotes.py <files…>; --show בראשית "ח כא" prints a verse. Run it before finishing any project. Note: the Psalms and Proverbs files use a hyphen-minus for maqaf, so keep the - in quotations from them.
  • ebl_fetch.py (fixed 2026-10-16): notes are now taken from the JSON (the ATF omits many), and range lines (66-67) are labeled.

More tools (2026-10-16, creation corpus):

  • ebl_fetch.py (fixed again): a line with several variant reconstructions now prints all of them (N (variant, other manuscripts):) with their manuscripts; before, the second variant and its manuscripts were silently dropped. Re-run it on older eBL folders if a line looks incomplete.
  • Project-level verification pattern (סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/1-אנומה-אליש/verify.py): checks the annotated entries against eBL's line list, the translation lines against the annotated > lines, every pair of eBL "parallel lines" (bracket-only differences listed separately), and a fixed passage against its table in renderings.md. Copy and adapt it for any eBL-based multi-tablet project. The same folder has build_translation.py (one reading file from per-tablet files) and build_parallels_index.py (merges per-tablet parallels tables into the corpus parallels-index.md, ordered by verse).

More tools (2026-10-16, creation corpus project 2):

  • seal2md.py: a saved SEAL text page → Markdown (catalogue fields; the text table line by line, with bilingual continuation lines marked ↳; SEAL's per-word lemmas; the translation). python3 -I tools/seal2md.py <node-N.html> <out.md> <url>. SEAL returns an error page to curl's default User-Agent: download with a browser UA (see the docstring).
  • cdl2md.py --morph: the ORACC converter now prints each word's ePSD2 morph and base ({ba.n.da:~;a,bi.a;nud}), the Sumerian "check the stem" (§4.6).
  • check_bible_quotes.py (fixed 2026-10-17): the loose book key dropped every י and ו, so יהושע resolved to הושע; it now keeps the first letter and tries the exact name first.
  • eBL fragmentarium transliteration search: GET /api/fragments/query?transliteration=<signs> finds every fragment with a sign sequence (e.g. ul-le-gar-ra → VAT 9307 = KAR 4). Use it to look for duplicates of a text before declaring it single-manuscript.
  • Project-level verify.py for a multi-text project (סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/2-טקסטי-בריאה-ועדן/verify.py): per text, checks the annotated entries against the edition's line list (eBL reading edition or ETCSL transliteration) and the translation lines against the annotated > lines; build_translation.py there joins per-text files.

More tools (2026-10-17, law and treaty corpus):

  • cdl2md.py --norm: adds a norm: line (the project's normalization of each word; SAAo, RINAP etc.) and prints the contextual sense after the guide word ([(treaty-)oath=treaty]).

  • oracc_html2tr.py: a saved ORACC per-text HTML view → Markdown translation (units labelled with the transliteration lines they span, section headings as ##). python3 -I tools/oracc_html2tr.py <in.html> <out.md> <title> <url>. Use it for any ORACC project: the zips have no translations.

  • Project tools in חוקים-ובריתות/1-אמנת-הירושה-של-אסרחדון/: build_data.py + make_parts.py (align a composite with a later copy by the SAAo labels and cut per-part data files for the translators), verify.py (entries, one > per entry, reserved words, fixed formulas and key-lemma roots, identical normalizations), build_translation.py (clean translation with § headings and footnotes from a הערת שוליים field), build_parallels_index.py (corpus index, Deuteronomy grouped by chapter).

  • sources_sync.py (2026-10-21): re-obtains the git-ignored sources. status / fetch / verify (work tier by default; --all adds the archive tier of old scans and photos; --only REGEX, --dest DIR, --jobs N); snapshot rewrites sources/MANIFEST.json where the files are. The recipes are in sources/fetch-recipes.tsv. It reports CHANGED when an online edition changed since our copy, and names the hosts blocked by a cloud allowlist. Text files are compared with their "generated/retrieved" dates blanked. Never extracts .exe/.dll from a zip. snapshot in a partial checkout (a cloud session without the archive tier, or with files that are CHANGED) drops the absent items and re-stamps the changed ones: there, add only the new items to the committed manifest (as the lead did on 2026-10-21). On a certificate error it retries with the public intermediates in tools/certs/ (ORACC omits its intermediate; 2026-10-21), then falls back to curl with the same certificates.

When you write a tool that another session could reuse, put it here with a usage docstring and add a row to this table.

More tools (2026-10-17, the Laws of Hammurabi):

  • cdli_composite2md.py: a CDLI composite ATF with #tr.ts / #tr.en lines → Markdown, optionally aligned line by line with one witness ATF (stele/tablet) by the transliteration sequence, and a JSON-lines file. Get the ATF from https://cdli.earth/artifacts/<id>/json ([0]['inscription']['atf']; witnesses' ATF inside [0]['witnesses']). python3 -I tools/cdli_composite2md.py <composite.atf> <out.md> <title> <url> [--witness <w.atf> <siglum>] [--jsonl <out>].
  • Project tools in חוקים-ובריתות/2-חוקי-חמורבי/: lh_config.py (files, topics, composite parser, stele alignment, SEAL mapping), build_data.py (per-file translator data: composite + stele + SEAL lemmas + rank-3), verify.py (entries per file with placeholders, § sections against the composite, reserved words, formula patterns, identical normalizations, translation = > lines; --strict), build_translation.py (topic and § headings, footnotes, placeholders). Corpus builder חוקים-ובריתות/build_parallels_index.py merges every project's Part tables (Exodus and Deuteronomy by chapter); it replaces the project-1 builder.
  • check_bible_quotes.py (fixed 2026-10-17): references to דברי הימים א/ב were skipped; now matched.

Run brief: translator-brief--sumerian--5-7.md with …--shared-lemmas.txt.

More tools (2026-10-19, the wisdom corpus, in ספרות-החכמה-והצדיק-הסובל/): wisdom_config.py (files with eBL line ranges, so one eBL chapter can be split over several annotated files; eBL readers; the Gilgameš corpus's Hebrew for cross-corpus parallels) and wisdom_tools.py – pars KEY (eBL parallels incl. cross-text L I.4 links to Gilgameš, and identical normalizations, with the Hebrew already given), verify [KEY…] [--strict] (entries, translation = > lines, reserved strings licensed by an eBL lemma or a normalization token, vocalization traps gated by lemma, repeated lines), build (per-file and per-project clean translations generated from translation--intro-<KEY>.rtl.md + the annotated file; never edited by hand), grep '<regex>' [--gilg], lemma '<regex>' (how a lemma was rendered so far: the cheapest consistency tool); build_parallels_index.py (Job first, then Psalms, Qohelet, Proverbs, Lamentations, Isaiah, Jeremiah, the Torah). translator-brief.md there is the reusable brief for Akkadian eBL texts.

  • ebl_fetch.py (fixed 2026-10-22, Etana): a reconstruction line that opens with a logogram in another language (25. %sb U₄.1.KAM@v.TA.AM₃ | %n inaṣṣarū …) was not recognized (only %n was), so it was glued to the previous line as a "variant" and its own N was empty. Read-only (fetch only). Run with python3 -I.

  • tools/branches.py (2026-10-30, the branch-per-session rule, guidelines §5.1b): name N [M [K]]; status; start-round N (translation-round-N from origin/main, pushed and checked out); new-child BRANCH (pushes this branch – a round branch first merges origin/main – and creates the child's branch from it on origin; prints the source_revision); checkout BRANCH; sync (fast-forward, or rebase local commits); push; finish -m SUBJECT [--into-main] (merges the parent's new commits into this branch – stops on a conflict – pushes it, then pushes one squash commit, this branch's tree on the parent's tip, with the child's commit subjects in its body; a round goes into main only with --into-main). Deepens a shallow clone when it needs history. Never force-pushes or deletes. Tested 2026-10-30 on a local bare repo (a round, two runs, a sub-session, a shared-file conflict, main moving meanwhile). Run with python3 -I.

  • claude/quota-related-instructions.ts (repo root, generic – not part of this folder; 2026-10-30, guidelines §5.1): the quota's two time ranges and the gate. No arguments: the instructions, with the coming ranges' times; check '<rate_limit_info JSON>' → GO range=… agents=… (exit 0) or WAIT <UTC> … (exit 3); ranges [N]; at ISO [INFO]; selftest. One TypeScript file with a #!/usr/bin/env node shebang: run it as-is (../../claude/quota-related-instructions.ts …), no node needed – node 22.18+ runs a .ts file directly. Shabbat times from a local sunset calculation (Tel Aviv; within ~3 minutes of Hebcal).

Run with python3 -I.

The treebank has no line numbers: words are aligned by their letters (diacritics, elision, case ignored; οὐδέ = οὐ + δέ handled). Marks: whole-line <del> → del, <add> → add, <del> inside a line → part with [ ]. Any Perseus Greek text with a treebank (Homer, the Hymns, Herodotus) can use it.

  • tools/aed2md.py (2026-10-23, Round 4 run 3): AED-TEI (the TLA 2018 Egyptian corpus as TEI) → line data. lines FILE.xml [FROM [TO]], md FILE.xml OUT.md (a reading edition with each word's TLA lemma id, morphology and German gloss in context), tr FILE.xml [FROM [TO]] (the TLA's German sentence translation: rank 3, after drafting); as a library parse(path) / translations(path). Marks: [ ] lost, ( ) defective writing, ⟨ ⟩ omitted, { } superfluous, ⸢ ⸣ damaged, ? unclear, […] <gap/>. Caution: in the TLA a <gap/> can separate two analyses of one written stretch (Amenemope: every mid-line gap) – not a loss; egypt_tools.py prints it /. Run with python3 -I -B.

מילים-באבן/stone_tools.py (Round 5 run 4, 2026-10-31) – the inscriptions corpus

fill | verify [--strict] | build | translit KEY | selftest (keys MS AJ KH MH GZ MT CT; config TEXTS). Two modes: reading
(Hebrew, Moabite – verify checks that the vocalized reading has exactly the base's letters, in order, with the same letters
inside [ ]; niqqud, maqaf, final forms, spaces and punctuation ignored) and translation (Punic – reserved words with
their licensing Punic word, traps that must be vocalized, every numeral of the base in the translation). Bases are TSV
files (label<TAB>square script, no final forms) under sources/; the Latin transliteration is generated. build writes
the clean files (each line: the reading / translation, then the square-script line), the combined project files and
parallels-index.md. A model for any future epigraphic corpus (Aramaic, Phoenician, Ammonite).

More tools (2026-10-31, Round 5 run 5): אגדות-מלכים/kings_tools.py key CL (the Cuthaean Legend, five eBL chapters OBI OBII MBA MBB SB): the eBL machinery of ET generalized – ebl_chapter() takes the project's chapter list and eBL text number (textno), reads eBL's Parallels: of any L I.<n> text, and links a range ("31-33") line by line; RESERVED_CL (Etana's gates + מבול, מצבה, מלאכה (šipru), שואל(ת), גבור, מחה, זרע, צלם/דמות; never נפילים, מזבח, the Deut 18 words), TRAPS (Magan, Meluḫḫa, Kutha, Bēlet-ilī, Narām-Sîn), eight CL formulas; fill KEY (eBL's N into every `@` line of the project). build_parallels_index.py reads the CL tables. ספרות-החכמה-והצדיק-הסובל/wisdom_config.py: keys PM (the Poor Man, eBL category I) and PV, PO, OH, SP, WR (the fables), all in FILLED; wisdom_tools.py RESERVED rows for נקם, אטד, כבשה, עכביש; its build_parallels_index.py reads projects 7–8. Known gap: wisdom_tools.py pars does not resolve eBL's bare category-I links ("L I.11 16", no stage or chapter); verify's identical-normalization check covers them.

More tools (2026-10-21, printed rows; moved 2026-10-24): layout/rows-tool.ts – measures, proposes and checks the printed rows of a translation.rtl.md (its translation.rtl.layout.ts, through layout/translation-layout.ts - the translations' layout logic, beside it), in the same Chromium, fonts and A4 width as the PDF printer. It never writes the module: try and propose print the row starts as constants to put into it. node layout/rows-tool.ts status | report <file> [--text] [--widths] [--run=N] [--review] | try <file> --run=N --move=a>b | propose <file> [--fix] | check <file> | resolve <file> | template <file> [--rules] | compare <file> --with=<module> | md5 <file> | preview <file> --pages=2-4,9 --out=<dir>, and --layout=<module> / --out=<path>. npm run layout-status (in _RTL-EDITOR) lists every file whose layout is missing, obsolete (the file changed since), flagged or broken. Used by layout sessions; see layout/layout-guidelines.md §3.

A formula row is scoped to some keys by a [keys: …] marker in its Note cell (formula_scope()): F8 (pāi ייתן) applies to HL1, HL2, HLPT only; F18 now requires aššuli in its formula context; the root-כפר NEVER row is licensed by kupri- (\bkupr|\bku-up-r).
  • The rows tool in a cloud session (layout/rows-tool.ts): _RTL-EDITOR/node_modules is not in a fresh checkout – run npm ci --ignore-scripts && npx patch-package in _RTL-EDITOR, then, because the lock's Playwright 1.58 does not match the cloud's pre-installed Chromium, move node_modules/playwright and playwright-core aside and link node_modules/playwright to the global /opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright. node layout/rows-tool.ts status . then takes about 3 minutes for the whole folder.
